title: Load a plugin from a class name

blocks.text: A plugin system reads a class name from configuration and creates it: `Class.forName(name)`, then `getDeclaredConstructor()`, `setAccessible(true)` and `newInstance()`. Configuration can be wrong, so **check the class before creating anything**: it must be a `Plugin`, and an **abstract class or an interface** cannot be instantiated at all.

items: It returns a **new** instance of the named class, made with its no-arg constructor, **at any access level**.
It throws **`IllegalArgumentException`** for a name no class has, for a class that is **not a `Plugin`**, and for an **abstract** plugin class, in each case **without running any constructor**.
Any other reflective failure becomes an `IllegalStateException`.

cases.says: load("practice.PluginLoaderTest$DefaultPlugin") gives a new working plugin on each call, and an unknown name is IllegalArgumentException.
A plugin whose no-arg constructor is private still loads.
A class that does not implement Plugin is IllegalArgumentException, and its constructor never ran.
An abstract class implementing Plugin is IllegalArgumentException, not a failed creation.

concepts: An object is created from a configured class name with Class.forName, getDeclaredConstructor, setAccessible and newInstance.
An abstract class or an interface cannot be instantiated reflectively, so the class is checked before newInstance.
